pr.title: feat(github): read GitHub's native stacks behind stk.githubStacks
pr.body:
<!-- git-stk:description -->
GitHub shipped [native stacked pull requests](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-stacked-pull-requests-are-now-in-public-preview/) to public preview. The local half of `gh stack` duplicates what git-stk already does; what GitHub has that git-stk cannot produce is the **server-side stack object** - the stack map on every PR, per-layer diffs reviewed in parallel, and atomic stack merge. This makes git-stk first-class there: git-stk stays the local driver, GitHub owns the stack.

All of it is behind **`stk.githubStacks`, off by default** - the GitHub feature is in public preview, and off means today's behaviour byte for byte. GitLab, Gitea and the demo provider are untouched.

## What it does

- **Reads** the stack: `NativeStack` and `ReviewProvider::native_stack_for`, with a `None` default - the same optional-method pattern as `review_state`, so only `GitHubProvider` implements anything. It shells to `gh api`, so no new dependency, no HTTP client, no credential handling.
- **Registers** it: `submit --stack`/`--downstack` posts the ordered reviews to `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/stacks`, bottom first - the order the stack lands in. An existing stack is extended via `/stacks/{n}/add` rather than replaced; an unchanged one makes no call.
- **Merges** it GitHub's way: a stacked pull request cannot go through the endpoint `gh pr merge` uses, so `merge` uses `PUT /pulls/{n}/merge-async` and polls the returned uuid to completion.
- **Stops retargeting** what GitHub owns: a stacked pull request's base cannot be changed by hand, because GitHub moves each layer itself as the one below lands. `submit` and `cleanup` say so instead of claiming a change git-stk did not make.
- `repair` prefers the stack GitHub records to the review base and to ancestry - an ordering that was *stated* rather than inferred, survives a wiped `.git/config`, and is still right where a review has since been retargeted.

## Why merge and retarget are in the same PR

Registering is not additive. I probed it live on `git-stk-test-gh` before writing any of it, and both of these are hard refusals:

```
gh pr merge      -> This pull request is part of a stack and must be merged using
                    the asynchronous merge REST API. (mergePullRequest)
gh pr edit --base -> Cannot change the base branch because the pull request is part
                    of a stack. (updatePullRequest)
```

So registration alone would have handed an opted-in user a broken `git stk merge` **and** a broken `git stk submit`. The three land together or not at all. Findings written up in #306.

## Verified end to end

Against real GitHub, with `stk.githubStacks = true`:

```
git stk submit --stack   -> created #4 -> main, #5 -> e2e/one, registered #4 #5 as a stack
                            GET /stacks -> {"number":6,"base":"main","layers":[4,5]}
git stk submit --stack   -> idempotent: no re-registration, no retarget attempted
git stk merge -y         -> merged #4 via merge-async; GitHub retargeted #5 to main
git stk merge -y         -> merged #5; stack complete
```

Test repo left clean afterwards - branches deleted, no open PRs.

## Not changed

The local side. `restack`, `absorb`, worktrees, `undo`, and the `branch.<name>.stk*` metadata are all still git-stk's, and the cross-provider stack overview stays - it carries merged and closed history the native map does not, and GitLab and Gitea have no equivalent.
<!-- /git-stk:description -->

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #306
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: checks_not_green_error still recommends `git stk merge --auto`, which this PR makes refuse any review in a GitHub native stack, so the hint answers one refusal with another.
